solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Some forgot Sir Alan turned into Lord (6)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: forg(OT SIR A)lan, the run of letters spanning the words

annotation.surface: Someone called Sir Alan was forgotten and ended up a peer.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Alan looks like the lord, but a knight is not a lord and he is only the container of letters. ARISTO is short for aristocrat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a lord is one member of the titled class that the clipped word for aristocrat names.

entries.clue: In bed knackered again? (7)

blocks.note: having turned in for the night
exhausted a second time; the question mark allows a playful split of the word

annotation.surface: Someone exhausted all over again and back under the covers.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split RE-TIRED; knackered is British slang for exhausted.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed.

entries.clue: Bashful painter taking hour to finish wine (5)

indicators.note: the H is taken out of its place in SHY
a finish is the end of something, so the hour is carried to the end of the word

blocks.note: SHY, with its H taken away to be moved
RA = Royal Academician, the usual crossword painter
h = hour, now placed at the end

annotation.surface: A shy artist leaves it an hour before finishing off the wine.
annotation.walkthrough: SHY + RA would give SHYRA; the clue asks for the H to be carried to the finish, making SYRAH. 'Finish wine' reads as drinking up, but wine is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Syrah is a red grape and the wine made from it, also called Shiraz.

entries.clue: Spanish go on parts of golf course out of bounds (3)

indicators.note: the word loses its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a golf course is divided into holes

annotation.surface: A golfer being told to play on after hitting it out of bounds, perhaps in Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' is golf jargon in the surface but here means lose the edges. 'Go on' is the cheer of encouragement.
annotation.definitionFit: Olé is the Spanish shout of encouragement, as at a bullfight: a Spanish 'go on!'.

entries.clue: Rifle fire has spread to the front (7)

indicators.note: the front of the answer is where the first piece goes, so the spreading word is placed ahead of the firing word

blocks.note: as colours ran in the wash
to fire someone is to sack them

annotation.surface: A fire has spread forward towards the front line.
annotation.walkthrough: Rifle and fire suggest shooting, but rifle is a verb meaning search through and fire means dismiss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to search a place roughly, turning it over to steal.

entries.clue: Bill’s OK, sadly driven after Oscar’s taken by railway (5,6)

indicators.note: something taken by the railway is carried aboard it, so the O rides inside RY
after means following, so driven comes later in the answer than sadly

blocks.note: ry = railway
O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet, put inside RY
alas = sadly, regrettably
as in driven or sent mad

annotation.surface: Someone called Bill is fine but was sadly driven off after a man named Oscar was hit by a train.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a person; it is a parliamentary bill, which becomes law once the monarch gives it royal assent.
annotation.definitionFit: Royal assent is the monarch's formal approval, the final OK that turns a bill into an Act.

entries.clue: Simple, impressive housing for millions (2,7)

indicators.note: NOBLE holds PRO inside it

blocks.note: noble = grand, impressive
pro = for, in favour of; housed in NOBLE
m = million(s)

annotation.surface: An impressive development providing homes for millions of people.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is housing policy; 'housing' is the container and 'for' is a separate piece, PRO.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom used as an adjective: an easy task is described as causing no difficulty at all.

entries.clue: Affectionate seal burdened by publicity (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the seal sits beneath AD, carrying it

blocks.note: an ad is publicity
an O-ring is a rubber seal

annotation.surface: A cuddly seal weighed down by all its media attention.
annotation.walkthrough: Seal suggests the animal; it is the mechanical O-ring.
annotation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing great affection.

entries.clue: Recognised antelope by one of its sounds (4)

indicators.note: the antelope's name has more than one pronunciation, and one sounds like the answer

blocks.note: GNU, said with a silent G

annotation.surface: Someone identified an antelope by one of the noises it makes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Its sounds' reads as the animal's calls; it means the ways its name can be pronounced, since GNU is said both with and without the G.
annotation.definitionFit: A past-tense synonym: to know a face on sight is to identify it.

entries.clue: Nicked supporters upped and ran (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, FANS goes up, reading backwards

blocks.note: fans = supporters
fled = ran away

annotation.surface: Some football supporters stole something, then got up and ran off.
annotation.walkthrough: Nicked is British slang for stole, as is snaffled.
annotation.definitionFit: To snaffle something is to take it for yourself, to nick it.

entries.clue: Yet to iron out effect of bad press? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Laundry still to be ironed, with a pun on pressing clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Iron out' and 'press' tempt towards laundry; the definition is bad press in the sense of bad news coverage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by consequence: hostile newspaper coverage leaves a person famous for the wrong reasons.

entries.clue: Common type of piano part (5)

blocks.note: p = piano, softly, in music
an actor's part is a role

annotation.surface: An everyday kind of piano part in a score.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about music, but 'common type' is a person: an ordinary working-class one.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal clipping of proletarian, a working-class person, and 'common' carries the old snobbish sense of lower class.

entries.clue: Fellow greeting attack on castle in adventurous spirit (3,3,4,2,2)

indicators.note: in an across clue, the first pieces come on after, following, FORT

blocks.note: a castle is a fort
he = a male person, a fellow
hello = a greeting
a fit of coughing is an attack

annotation.surface: A man greets people while launching an assault on a castle, full of daring.
annotation.walkthrough: Attack goes with castle in the surface, but it is a fit, as of illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something for the hell of it means just for fun or adventure, with no other reason.

entries.clue: Scavenger slipping back off bin-bag in city (7,4)

indicators.note: the back of bin-bag is its last letter
the pieces go inside HULL

blocks.note: Hull is a city in Yorkshire
slipping up, making a mistake
the back of bin-baG

annotation.surface: A seagull slips away backwards off a rubbish bag in town.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the bird itself raiding the rubbish; 'slipping back' falls apart into ERRING and 'back off bin-bag', the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Herring gulls are notorious scavengers, raiding bins and landfill.

entries.clue: Swimming beaches west of Deal covered with sewage from east (5)

indicators.note: the westernmost letter of Deal, its first
D sits inside the other word
the sewage reads from the east, right to left

blocks.note: soil = sewage, as in a soil pipe; turned around to LIOS
first letter of Deal, placed inside

annotation.surface: Bathing beaches near the Kent town of Deal fouled with sewage from the east.
annotation.walkthrough: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, which makes the sewage scene painfully plausible; here it supplies only its D.
annotation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming place or bathing beach.

entries.clue: Booming speaker upset coach and umpire around court (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue each word is turned upside down, reading backwards
the reversed words go around WOO

blocks.note: a coach is a bus
to court someone is to woo them
ref = referee, an umpire

annotation.surface: A loud-mouthed person on court upset at the coach and umpire, like a tennis tantrum.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a shouting player; the speaker is hi-fi equipment.
annotation.definitionFit: A subwoofer is a loudspeaker for booming bass notes.

entries.clue: Dispatch delicate candle (9)

blocks.note: to send quickly
light as in a light touch

annotation.surface: Send off a fragile candle.
annotation.walkthrough: A rushlight is a historic cheap candle made of a rush dipped in fat.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind for the general word: a rush pith dipped in tallow burned like a cheap, thin candle.

entries.clue: Oddly stranded in that place with river rising, row across regularly? (5-3)

indicators.note: in a down clue the R moves up, earlier in the word

blocks.clueFragment: in that place with river rising
blocks.note: THERE, with its R (river) moved up a place
ferries ply across a stretch of water, travelling it regularly

annotation.surface: Someone stuck in a place as the river floods, rowing across and back again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stranded' suggests being marooned by the rising river; it means made of strands, and three is an odd number of them.
annotation.definitionFit: Three-ply wool or tissue has three strands or layers, an odd number.

entries.clue: Adjustment to dole is big inconvenience (9)

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A change to unemployment benefit causes real hardship.
annotation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit. 'Inconvenience' here is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To disoblige someone is to inconvenience them or refuse them a favour.

entries.clue: African, unused to water, has capsized out of trim yacht (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue HAS is turned upside down, reading backwards
TRIM is taken out of the yacht's name

blocks.note: HAS turned backwards
TRIMARAN, a yacht, with TRIM taken out

annotation.surface: A landlubber from Africa has overturned a yacht with its sails badly set.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of trim' is sailing jargon for badly balanced; it splits as 'out of' plus 'trim', and 'trim yacht' hides TRIMARAN. Unused to water extends the definition: a desert dweller.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone from the Sahara is African and, living in desert, unused to water.

entries.clue: Underground hacker is under 18, reportedly (5)

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the word is taken by how it is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a minor is someone under 18

annotation.surface: A secret teenage computer hacker is still a child.
annotation.walkthrough: Hacker and underground suggest computer crime; a miner hacks at rock below ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A miner works underground hacking out coal or ore.

entries.clue: Bananas eaten on delivery yesterday? (7)

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Bananas that got eaten on the day they were delivered.
annotation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like fruit being eaten; it means crazy. The definition is a baby delivered only yesterday.
annotation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, one delivered as recently as yesterday.

entries.clue: How cocaine gets in, sometimes at high rate (7,3,4)

blocks.note: cocaine is often snorted
describes paying an extortionate price

annotation.surface: A remark on drug taking, getting high at speed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High' tempts towards drugs; the second sense is a steep price.
annotation.definitionFit: Snorted cocaine goes up the nose, and paying through the nose means paying far too much.

entries.clue: Stand when fish bites (5)

indicators.note: the fish takes AS between its teeth, inside itself

blocks.note: the usual crossword fish
as = when, e.g. 'as I left'

annotation.surface: An angler stands up when a fish takes the bait.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb for the angler; it is a noun, the artist's stand.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: the artist's three-legged frame holds a canvas upright.

entries.clue: Ace is overturned with loud “You cannot be serious” (2,2)

indicators.note: in a down clue IS is turned upside down to SI

blocks.note: a = ace, on playing cards
IS turned backwards
f = forte, loud in music

annotation.surface: A tennis ace is overruled and the player shouts John McEnroe's famous protest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You cannot be serious' was McEnroe's outburst at Wimbledon, which ties ace and overturned to tennis.
annotation.definitionFit: 'As if!' is a scornful retort meaning you cannot be serious.

entries.clue: Line at end of letter triggers turning over (5)

indicators.note: the word is turned round, reading backwards

blocks.note: triggers a gun, fires it

annotation.surface: The final line of a letter makes someone flip their lid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of letter' suggests the sign-off of a written letter; it is a letter of type.
annotation.definitionFit: A serif is the short line finishing a stroke of a printed letter.

entries.clue: Clear system of exchanges applied to Tallinn’s university (9)

indicators.note: letters exchange places, a rearrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
u = university, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A new telephone exchange system introduced at the university in Tallinn, capital of Estonia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear' is a computer verb here: remove software.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing sense of clear: removing software from a device.

entries.clue: Kind KC yields initial point (3)

indicators.note: gives up its first letter

blocks.note: a King's Counsel is a senior barrister, known as a silk
S = south, a compass point, and the initial dropped from SILK

annotation.surface: A generous barrister concedes the opening point of an argument.
annotation.walkthrough: Kind looks like an adjective praising the KC; it is a noun, sort. KCs wear silk gowns, hence silk.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym meaning sort or type, heard mostly in phrases like 'people of that sort'.

entries.clue: Time left after sport for passing practice? (7)

indicators.note: after means following, so the time and left pieces follow the sport piece

blocks.note: sport as in fun, play
an era is a period of time
l = left

annotation.surface: Leftover time after a match used for passing drills in training.
annotation.walkthrough: Passing practice sounds like a football drill; the question mark allows it to mean the rites for someone who has passed away.
annotation.definitionFit: A funeral is the customary practice held when someone passes on.

entries.clue: Hitman gets Tesla for one pound in good condition (6)

indicators.note: 'for' means in exchange for, so T is traded in for one of the two Ls

blocks.note: a hitman is a paid killer
T = tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
l = pound (libra), swapped out for T

annotation.surface: A contract killer gets a Tesla car for one pound, still running well.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker; it is the scientific unit, symbol T.
annotation.definitionFit: Kilter means good working order, as in out of kilter.
